A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including renumbered and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 13 base LMMs across ten datasets, alongside prompting, reasoning, agreement and prediction-error experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations of larger and commercial models in Appendix A.4, Tables 10–11.

M1.justification: The classification procedure, four metrics, error-group thresholds and prompting/reasoning interventions remain unchanged. Additional pretrained models extend the evaluated comparison set without introducing a proposed method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten classification datasets and four task groups. The additional comparisons reuse this coverage; the commercial-model experiment uses five existing datasets without introducing a new task or input scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 10–11 substantially expand the evaluated comparison set with six larger variants: InstructBLIP 13B, InternVL2 26B, LLaVA-1.5 13B, LLaVA-NeXT Vicuna 13B and Yi 34B, and Qwen2VL 72B. They also introduce GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, Claude Haiku 3.5, Claude Sonnet 3.5 and Gemini 2.0 Flash. Existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: The added experiments extend model-size configurations to 13B–72B and report a commercial-model comparison averaged over Caltech101, DTD, Flowers102, OxfordPets and UCF101. Existing splits, metrics, prompts and testing procedures are not revised.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4 adds an explicit larger-versus-smaller model comparison examining whether scaling consistently helps, supported by Table 10. Existing prompting, reasoning, label-ambiguity, agreement and Elo analyses remain intact; the new training-factor hypotheses are discussion rather than controlled ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point-estimate reporting and the same 10,000-pair sampling procedure for Elo evaluation. No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests are added or removed.

E6.justification: Tables 10–11 add substantial results for previously unevaluated models while preserving existing result tables. For example, Table 10 reports fine-grained TI of 36.5 for InternVL2 26B versus 22.3 for 8B. Table 11 reports five-dataset LI of 77.3 for Claude Sonnet 3.5. It also introduces an inconsistency: InstructBLIP 7B has LI 38.3 and SS 37.4, whereas its retained per-dataset scores in Tables 6–7 imply approximately 47.5 and 43.6.

T1.justification: The formal task and metric definitions are unchanged. Equation 1 replaces 'pr' with the existing prediction notation, a notational correction without changing the inclusion rule. No substantive assumptions, derivations or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: evaluating 13 base models across ten datasets using four metrics, analyzing prediction errors, and exploring prompting and reasoning remedies. The appendix additions do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.4 adds interpretations of mixed scaling effects and competitive open/commercial performance, plus hypotheses concerning vision pretraining, image resolution, training strategy and data. It newly acknowledges that incomplete training disclosures impede attribution. These extend the discussion without revising the existing error interpretations.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4 identifies the Vicuna/Yi backbones of added LLaVA-NeXT variants and supplies author-estimated commercial-model sizes. The existing model-summary table, prompt documentation, split information and code-access statement remain unchanged; detailed commercial API configurations are not supplied.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, novelty positioning and 74 bibliography entries are retained. Changed citation back-references reflect pagination and added uses of existing references.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgements and three discussion blocks within Appendix A.4, updates cross-references and corrects the TI notation. The main narrative and section sequence are otherwise retained, without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 10–11 with color distinctions for larger and commercial models, relocates Figure 8 between columns and reflows appendix displays. Existing figures retain their content; v1 Tables 10–17 become v2 Tables 12–19 with unchanged results.

improvement.justification: Tables 10–11 improve empirical relevance by extending the comparisons to larger and commercial models while preserving the original analyses. The gain is modest: training-versus-size explanations remain confounded, commercial sizes are only estimates, and Table 11 introduces an InstructBLIP 7B averaging inconsistency.
